title: How Paul's Words Traveled
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Sort twelve dated events from 386 to 1999 into four strands of Paul's later influence on a timeline, and see Martin Luther land in three of them.

educational.topic: Paul's Later Influence and Contested Legacy
learningObjectives: Organize twelve dated events from 386 CE to 1999 into four strands of Paul's later influence (grace and faith; conscience and equality; contempt and its repudiation; rereading Paul), placing at least 10 of 12 in the correct strand.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Categorize on a timeline: drag fixed-date event cards into four thematic strands, one scored Check with reasoned feedback
keyQuestions: Which of Paul's ideas did each event carry forward, or fight over?
Why does Martin Luther appear in three different strands?
When does the contempt strand turn toward repudiation, and what came just before?
commonMisconceptions: Paul's influence ran in one direction, either all good or all harmful.
Each historical figure belongs to one strand; in fact Luther appears in three.
Scholarly rereading of Paul is a recent fad with no history; it began in the 1960s and 1970s.
The Reformation was about conscience alone; its starting point was grace.
assessmentOpportunities: At least 10 of 12 events placed in the correct strand on the first Check.
Explain, using the timeline, why Paul's legacy is called contested.
